reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let n be a positive integer, let h be a nonnegative integer, and let x=(x_0,…,x_h) be any fixed tuple of vectors in ℝ^n. Write [m]={0,…,m−1}, let L=[h+1], and put D=2^{64(h+1)}, M=2^{74(h+1)}, and P={p∈ℕ : p is even and 4≤p≤D}. For each i∈L let q_i=h−i+1, J_i={(j,k) : j∈[q_i], k∈[M^j]}, S_i=∑_{j∈[q_i]} M^j, and t_{i,j}=x_{i+j} for j∈[q_i]. For i∈L and p∈P let C_{i,p} be the set of all maps [p]×J_i→[n], and set
a_{i,p}=1/(p^4 S_i^2 √(q_i log(2 D S_i))),
where log is the natural logarithm. Define ϕ(t)=exp(−1/t) for t>0 and ϕ(t)=0 for t≤0, and set
χ(r)=[ϕ(r−13/20)/(ϕ(r−13/20)+ϕ(7/10−r))] [ϕ(1−r)/(ϕ(1−r)+ϕ(r−19/20))],
c_i=∏_{j∈[q_i]} χ(‖t_{i,j}‖/√n).
For any u=(u_j)_{j∈[q_i]} in (ℝ^n)^{q_i} and z∈ℝ^{C_{i,p}}, define
G_{i,p}(u,z)=√n a_{i,p} ∑_{f∈C_{i,p}} z_f ∏_{(ℓ,(j,k))∈[p]×J_i} (u_j)_{f(ℓ,(j,k))}.
Let Ω=ℝ^{⨆_{(i,p)∈L×P} C_{i,p}}, with its standard Euclidean structure, and let ξ have the standard Gaussian law on Ω. Write ξ_{i,p}=(ξ_{(i,p),f})_{f∈C_{i,p}} for its (i,p)-block, without any rescaling. Define H(ξ)_i=0 if some t_{i,j}=0; otherwise, with u_j=t_{i,j}/‖t_{i,j}‖, define
H(ξ)_i=c_i ∑_{p∈P} G_{i,p}(u,ξ_{i,p}).
Then H is almost-everywhere measurable under the standard Gaussian law on Ω, and its pushforward law is the product over i∈L of the centered real Gaussian laws of variance
v_i=max{0, n c_i^2 ∑_{p∈P} a_{i,p}^2}=n c_i^2 ∑_{p∈P} a_{i,p}^2.
In particular, the coordinates H(ξ)_i are independent, with a point mass at zero when v_i=0.
objects: A deterministic tuple x, its level tails t_{i,j}, the smooth cutoff χ and its products c_i, the weights a_{i,p}, the multilinear Gaussian coefficient expression G_{i,p}, the block-indexed standard Gaussian ξ, and the output vector H(ξ).
domains: n∈ℕ_{>0}, h∈ℕ, x∈(ℝ^n)^{h+1}; i∈L=[h+1], p∈P={even p∈ℕ : 4≤p≤D}, j∈[q_i], k∈[M^j], and ℓ∈[p], where [m]={0,…,m−1}. C_{i,p} is the set of maps [p]×J_i→[n]; z∈ℝ^{C_{i,p}}, ξ∈Ω=ℝ^{⨆_{(i,p)}C_{i,p}}, and H(ξ)∈ℝ^L.
quantifiers: For every positive n, every nonnegative h, and every deterministic x∈(ℝ^n)^{h+1}, the asserted law holds for H under ξ∼N(0,I_Ω). Each coordinate's zero-tail condition quantifies over j∈[q_i]; all finite sums and products range over their full stated index sets.
assumptions: The only requirements on the deterministic inputs are positivity of n, h being a natural number, and x being a tuple of the prescribed length and dimension. ξ is distributed according to the standard Gaussian on Ω. There are no nonzero-tail or tail-norm assumptions; the zero-tail test defines the field, and the parity and bounds on p define an index set.
conclusion: H is almost-everywhere measurable under the standard Gaussian on Ω and pushes it forward to the product over i∈L of Gaussian laws with mean zero and variance (n c_i^2 ∑_{p∈P} a_{i,p}^2) truncated below at zero, which is already nonnegative. The output coordinates are independent; a zero variance gives a Dirac mass at zero.
scopes: D, M, L and P are global for fixed h. The tail indices, J_i, S_i, and c_i are level-local. Each a_{i,p} and coefficient block is specific to (i,p). If a level has a zero tail vector, only that level's formula takes the zero branch; otherwise the tail is normalized before use. The sole random input is ξ, with separate disjoint coordinate blocks, and the law is joint across all levels.
constant_dependencies: D=2^{64(h+1)} and M=2^{74(h+1)} depend only on h; p ranges over even degrees from 4 through D inclusive. q_i=h−i+1 and S_i=∑_{j=0}^{q_i−1}M^j. a_{i,p}=(p^4 S_i^2 √(q_i log(2 D S_i)))^{−1} depends on h,i,p and not n or x. The cutoff uses 13/20, 7/10, 19/20 and 1 with ϕ(t)=exp(−1/t) for positive t and 0 otherwise; c_i depends on the tail through ‖x_{i+j}‖/√n. G_{i,p} has prefactor √n a_{i,p}, and the variance uses n c_i^2 times the sum of squared weights.
